The Fall of Lucifer
thuh FAWL of LOO-si-fur
noun phrase (demonology)
The doctrine of Satan's original fall from his holy estate through pride and rebellion. The name Lucifer (Latin light-bearer, from the Vulgate rendering of Hebrew helel, day star / shining one, Isaiah 14:12) became the traditional name for the pre-fall Satan. The classic prooftexts (Isaiah 14:12-15; Ezekiel 28:12-19) are debated as to their precise reference.

📖 Biblical Definition

The doctrine of Satan's original fall from his holy estate through pride and rebellion against God. The name Lucifer (Latin lux + ferre, light-bearer) derives from the Vulgate's rendering of the Hebrew helel ben-shachar (day star, son of the morning / shining one) in Isaiah 14:12, and became the traditional name for the pre-fall Satan. The classic prooftexts and their interpretive debate: (1) Isaiah 14:12-15, How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!... For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God... I will be like the most High. Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell; the immediate context is a taunt against the king of Babylon (Isaiah 14:4), but the language has traditionally been understood (by many of the Fathers and the Reformers) as also describing, by extension or typologically, the fall of Satan through pride. (2) Ezekiel 28:12-19, the lament over the king of Tyre, describing one who was perfect in beauty... in Eden the garden of God... the anointed cherub... perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee... thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty; again the immediate context is the king of Tyre, but the language (the cherub in Eden, perfect till iniquity was found) has traditionally been understood as describing, by extension, the fall of Satan. The substantive doctrine, whether or not these specific texts directly describe Satan's fall, is established by the broader biblical witness: Satan was created holy (as all the angels were, the original very-good creation, Genesis 1:31); he fell through pride and rebellion (1 Timothy 3:6 warns against the novice elder being lifted up with pride and falling into the condemnation of the devil, indicating pride as the cause of the devil's fall); he became the adversary, the chief of the fallen angels. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive doctrine of Satan's fall through pride with appropriate exegetical care regarding the Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28 prooftexts (acknowledging the immediate human-king referents while recognizing the traditional extended application to Satan), and notes the substantive moral lesson: pride was the cause of the devil's fall, and pride remains the great peril (the warning of 1 Timothy 3:6; Proverbs 16:18, pride goeth before destruction).

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The doctrine of Satan's original fall from his holy estate through pride and rebellion; the name Lucifer (Latin light-bearer) from the Vulgate rendering of Isaiah 14:12; the classic prooftexts (Isaiah 14:12-15; Ezekiel 28:12-19) debated as to precise reference; pride the cause of the devil's fall (1 Timothy 3:6).

THE FALL OF LUCIFER, n. phr. (demonology) Satan's original fall from his holy estate through pride and rebellion. Lucifer (Latin light-bearer) from the Vulgate rendering of Hebrew helel (day star, son of the morning, Isaiah 14:12). Classic prooftexts (debated): Isaiah 14:12-15 (How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer... I will exalt my throne above the stars of God... I will be like the most High; immediate context the king of Babylon, traditionally applied also to Satan); Ezekiel 28:12-19 (the king of Tyre as the anointed cherub in Eden, perfect till iniquity was found; traditionally applied also to Satan). The broader witness establishes: Satan created holy (Genesis 1:31); fell through pride (1 Timothy 3:6, the condemnation of the devil). Pride the cause of the fall (Proverbs 16:18).

📖 Key Scripture

Isaiah 14:12-14 — "How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!... For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God... I will be like the most High."

Ezekiel 28:15-17 — "Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee... thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness."

1 Timothy 3:6 — "Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil."

Luke 10:18 — "And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The doctrine of Satan's fall through pride is established by the broader biblical witness; the Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28 prooftexts require exegetical care (immediate human-king referents with traditional extended application to Satan).

expand to see more

The fall of Lucifer as a doctrine requires appropriate exegetical care. The two classic prooftexts (Isaiah 14:12-15 and Ezekiel 28:12-19) have immediate referents that are human kings — the king of Babylon (Isaiah 14:4) and the king of Tyre (Ezekiel 28:12) — and some modern interpreters hold that these texts refer only to the human kings, not to Satan. The traditional interpretation (held by many of the Fathers and the Reformers) recognizes the immediate human-king referents while understanding the language (the fall from heaven, the ascent above the stars of God, the anointed cherub in Eden, the perfection till iniquity was found) as also describing, by extension or typologically, the fall of Satan through pride. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive doctrine with this exegetical care: whether or not these specific texts directly describe Satan's fall, the broader biblical witness establishes that Satan was created holy, fell through pride and rebellion, and became the chief of the fallen angels (1 Timothy 3:6 explicitly attributes the devil's condemnation to pride; Luke 10:18, the Lord Jesus beholding Satan fall as lightning from heaven). The substantive moral lesson is sobering and central: pride was the cause of the devil's fall, and pride remains the great peril for men and especially for those in spiritual office (1 Timothy 3:6; Proverbs 16:18, pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall). The doctrine warns the believer against the pride that destroyed the highest of the angels.

Lucifer (Latin light-bearer) from the Vulgate of Isaiah 14:12; Satan's fall through pride; Isaiah 14:12-15 and Ezekiel 28:12-19 (debated); 1 Timothy 3:6 (pride the cause); Luke 10:18.
